Topic: Mastering Bayes' Theorem and Independence

Target audience: University students (Introductory Statistics/Data Science)

Section: section_1 — Prerequisite Warm-up: Conditional Probability

Lecture lines:
Conditional probability focuses on a reduced sample space.
Think of it as zooming into event B.
We only count outcomes where both A and B happen.

Planned animations:
Fade in rectangle representing full sample space #FFFFFF.
Highlight subset B (dog owners) with color #FF9900.
Highlight overlapping subset A (cat owners) with color #00CCFF.
Zoom in on the intersection A and B.
Final label showing P(A|B) as the ratio of intersection.

Section: section_2 — The Concept of Independence

Lecture lines:
Independence means knowing B gives no info on A.
The probability of A remains unchanged by B.
Visually, the ratio of A is constant throughout.

Planned animations:
Show two coin flip outcomes #FFFFFF.
Display P(A|B) = P(A) formula in #FFFF00.
Animate ratio of A remaining constant despite change in B.

Section: section_3 — Introducing Bayes' Theorem

Lecture lines:
Bayes' Theorem updates beliefs with new evidence.
Think like a sniffer dog seeking truth.
Start with a prior belief.
Adjust it based on new likelihood data.
Arrive at a refined posterior probability.

Planned animations:
Display Prior probability tree with branches #FFCC00.
Introduce Evidence node with color #00FF00.
Animate flow from Prior to Posterior using Bayes formula #FFFFFF.
Highlight calculated Posterior with bold #FF0000.
Show final state: updated belief based on Evidence.

Section: section_4 — Integration: When Bayes Meets Independence

Lecture lines:
Independence makes Bayesian calculations much simpler.
Joint probabilities become simple products of individual terms.
This acceleration is vital for real-time systems.

Planned animations:
Display complex joint probability formula in #FFFFFF.
Animate simplification process highlighting independence.
Show final product P(A) * P(B) in #00FF00.

Section: section_5 — Summary & Application Loop

Lecture lines:
Independence simplifies computation significantly.
Bayes' Theorem provides the logic for learning.
Together, they power modern data classifiers.

Planned animations:
Show loop icon connecting Independence to Bayes #FFCC00.
Animate email filter nodes with color #00CCFF.
Display 'Spam' or 'Ham' classification text in #FFFFFF.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")

        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject
